gen-fs-gambarino-poppins: Poppins keeps its curves loose and tall, with no shading at all. Gambarino is the showman, heavy black stems against razor hairlines, while Poppins just lets the words run along smoothly.
gen-fs-gambarino-work-sans: Work Sans reads with a high, tidy line and open-tipped curves. Gambarino's heavy stems and hairline strokes give the page drama, and the sans beneath them simply keeps the text moving.
gen-fs-hoover-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Hoover's e has a wide, funnel-shaped throat that you notice right away. Be Vietnam Pro follows with a uniform, bent-rod stroke, so long paragraphs move along without any fuss.
gen-fs-hoover-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab fills the middle of each line with dense, structured texture. Hoover's bookish serif sits above it, and a long passage would feel steady, with open a, c, e and s keeping the rhythm easy.
gen-fs-kalam-instrument-sans: Cozy is the first impression, thanks to Kalam's hand-drawn, tightly bundled lines. Instrument Sans brings a crisp, unvarying stroke with open pincer-like c shapes, and that gap between hand and machine is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-fs-kalam-montserrat: Inviting and homey, Kalam looks drawn by hand and packed close together. Montserrat's wire-light line and oversized, generous counters spread out beneath it, so the page feels both personal and spacious.
gen-fs-karma-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads as curvy and loose, with a wire-thin skeleton and stubby ascender tips on tall-bodied letters. Karma's gently thickened curves above it make a longer read feel warm.
gen-fs-karma-fs-merriweather-sans: Soft curves, sturdy words. Karma's modest stress and see-through s sit over Merriweather Sans, and its tall lowercase and clearly open e make a long stretch of text feel dependable.
gen-fs-karma-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad, open counters. Karma does its best work in the mild letterpress-like shading of its curves, while Public Sans simply delivers solid, low-contrast text.
gen-fs-karma-gf-cascadia-code: Rounded and relaxed, Karma shows a see-through s and curves that thicken at the shoulders. Cascadia Code, wire-thin and widely spaced, is the opposite, and that tension between shaded serif and uniform monoline is the pair's strongest quality.
